Great to meet earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so procurement has what you need to route a PR:

2) Marketplace vs direct vendor: you said Marketplace (Coupa) is preferred if we can map a supplier ID; if marketplace path isn’t an option we’ll do direct vendor setup (Ariba also acceptable).
3) Supplier onboarding items you requested: W-9, bank details, and Redwood vendor packet. Attached is our standard PR template for your AP team (redwood_pr_template.xlsx) and a short vendor packet.

Actions I’ll take:
- Share PR template and vendor packet (attached).
- Open an internal ticket to start supplier mapping and confirm whether we already exist in your Coupa catalog.

Could you confirm:
- Coupa vs Ariba (you said Coupa but want to confirm the tenant/team).
- Whether Acme needs a Redwood legal contact or a vendor contact for onboarding (I can loop in our finance manager).
- Expected timeline for assigning a supplier ID (estimate works).

Thanks — I’ll coordinate on our side and copy Avery (ops) and Priyom (solutions eng) for the technical bits.

Best,

Hi Soojin —

Thanks for the summary. Confirming the procurement details from my side:

- We use Coupa (global tenant: acme-coupa). Marketplace is preferred since it speeds processing and avoids a manual vendor add.
- AP prefers to issue a standard PO on net-30 terms. If you need different terms we can escalate, but net-30 is the default.
- Typical supplier ID assignment: 3–7 business days after we receive vendor docs (W-9, bank info).

What we need from Redwood to start:
- Completed vendor onboarding form (I attached our example in a follow-up so you can see required fields).
- W-9 and bank details (for EFT).
- Confirmation of Redwood legal name and remit address (exact text for Coupa).

I’ll also open a Coupa Supplier Request once we have the vendor packet. If you can confirm the exact legal name and remit address in your next note, that’s most helpful.

Lara Boone
Senior Procurement Manager | Acme Industries
procurement@acme-industries.com
